findings.specText: story-023 (contract NatSpec, HEAD 7045a96): "Recovery note: reward forwarding uses safeTransfer, so a recipient that cannot receive the reward token (e.g. a blocklisted address) reverts the batch. As with MigratorV1V2, the operational escape is to exclude such addresses from the seed list (or deploy and re-wire a fresh migrator)" — and earlier: "once a pass has completed (migrateIterator == -1) the owner may call seedUsers again with a fresh straggler list. Reseeding mid-pass is forbidden."
findings.actualBehavior: The story offers 'exclude such addresses from the seed list' as the primary operational escape from the reverting-recipient brick, but the code's own reseed guard require(!seeded || migrateIterator == -1) (line 114) — reinforced by the story's own line 'Reseeding mid-pass is forbidden' — makes that escape UNREACHABLE while the pass is bricked: a safeTransfer revert to a frozen recipient (lines 187/190/193) reverts the whole migrate chunk, the cursor stays pinned at that index so migrateIterator can never reach -1, and withdrawAll deliberately does NOT reset the pass (lines 210-229). Excluding the address requires a reseed that the guard forbids until -1, which the brick prevents. Only the secondary escape (deploy + re-wire a fresh migrator via setMigrator on both V2 and V3) actually works.
findings.deviation: Spec self-contradiction: the documented recovery path ('exclude from the seed list') is contradicted by the same document's mid-pass reseed prohibition and the code's reseed guard. The story overstates in-contract recoverability; the true recovery is only a full redeploy.
findings.securityRelevance: Same underlying brick as code-scanner MIG-LOCAL-01 (griefable liveness DoS of the whole migration by one blocklisted/reverting reward recipient, realistic for USDC/USDT stable rewardToken). Funds are not stolen or permanently stuck (users retain their V2 positions; withdrawAll recovers stranded balances), so this is a recoverable liveness hazard, not a Law-1 fund-loss escalation. The Law-2 contribution here is the false/contradictory recovery claim; severity of the DoS itself is owned by the code/econ scanner.

findings.specText: story-022 (Phase 3 + batchClaim NatSpec, line 435): "Failed transfers (e.g. blocklisted recipients) are banked into unclaimablePromo — the flush must never brick." Header design principle (lines 26-35): rotation is a "cursor-guaranteed batchClaim flush" whose completeness is load-bearing.
findings.specSource: src/PhlimboV3.sol NatSpec + SolvencyDetermination.md 4 (banked failed-transfer invariant), git commit 7045a96
findings.actualBehavior: The 'never brick' principle is implemented for outright transfer FAILURE (batchClaim banks pending into unclaimablePromo, lines 458-464), and that banking logic is itself faithful. However the non-reverting primitive _tryTransfer (lines 816-820) does abi.decode(returndata, (bool)) with no length check: a promo token that returns non-empty returndata SHORTER than 32 bytes causes abi.decode to REVERT, which propagates out of _tryTransfer and reverts the entire batchClaim chunk — bricking the flush it was designed to protect. finalizePromotion then cannot be reached (flushCursor cannot advance past that staker), stranding the rotation in Flushing (unpause also blocked).
findings.deviation: The stated invariant 'the flush must never brick' does not fully hold: it survives compliant failing transfers but not a non-standard/short-returndata promo token. The banking design is faithful; the decode edge case undermines it.
findings.securityRelevance: Duplicate of code-scanner V3-LOCAL-01. Mitigated by the owner-vetted-promo-token trust assumption (partner tokens are vetted per promotion), so likelihood is low; primary ownership and severity sit with the code scanner. Flagged here only because it contradicts an explicitly documented design principle.
